questions.prompt: You accidentally sent UPI money to the wrong person. What is your safest first step?

options.text: Beg or argue with the stranger in chat
options.explanationWrong: Pleading or arguing with strangers often triggers release-fee scams.

options.text: Save the transaction ID and take a screenshot as proof
Send another ₹100 to 'unlock' an automatic refund
options.explanationWrong: Paying extra to unlock a refund is a classic follow-up scam.

options.text: Delete the receipt so it does not confuse your bank
options.explanationWrong: You need the transaction reference number to raise any official dispute.

questions.explanationCorrect: Save your proof first—every official complaint with your payment app, bank, or NPCI requires the transaction ID.

questions.prompt: Where should you file the first official dispute for a wrong UPI transfer?

options.text: Inside the payment app you used, and with your bank
By commenting on a social media thread
options.explanationWrong: Public posts cannot reverse payments and can attract fake 'recovery agents'.

options.text: Wait 30 days silently to see if it auto-reverses
options.explanationWrong: Delaying reduces recovery chances; report as soon as possible.

options.text: Call a number sent by the recipient claiming to be a 'refund desk'
options.explanationWrong: Never trust numbers sent by the stranger who received the funds.

questions.explanationCorrect: Log the wrong-transfer complaint directly inside your payment app and contact your bank's official 24×7 helpline.

questions.prompt: Your payment app and bank have not resolved your wrong transfer complaint. Where can you escalate officially?

options.text: Pay a 'cyber recovery expert' you found on Telegram
options.explanationWrong: Self-proclaimed recovery agents asking upfront fees are almost always scams.

options.text: Escalate through the NPCI UPI dispute redressal process
Share your UPI PIN with a third-party website to pull the money back
options.explanationWrong: No website can pull money back using your PIN—they will drain your account instead.

options.text: Send a collect request with a warning note
options.explanationWrong: Strangers do not have to approve collect requests; use official banking channels.

questions.explanationCorrect: If your PSP app and bank do not resolve the ticket, escalate through NPCI's official dispute redressal portal and Banking Ombudsman.

questions.prompt: The stranger who got your wrong transfer says: 'Send ₹500 release fee and I will refund the full amount.' What is this?

options.text: A secondary scam—never pay extra money to get a refund
Standard bank clearing charge for UPI reversals
options.explanationWrong: Banks and UPI apps never ask customers to pay strangers a 'release fee'.

options.text: A mandatory NPCI escrow step
options.explanationWrong: NPCI never charges a fee through a stranger's UPI handle.

options.text: Safe if they promise in writing
options.explanationWrong: Scammers gladly send fake written receipts to steal more.

questions.explanationCorrect: Never pay a 'release fee' or 'tax' to recover lost money. That is a common follow-up trick to double your loss.

questions.prompt: Why does raising a wrong-credit complaint quickly with your bank matter?

options.text: Your bank can formally notify the recipient's bank while funds may still be traceable
Your bank can reverse any transaction without contacting the other bank
options.explanationWrong: Reversals require coordination through the receiving bank and official dispute workflow.

options.text: Because UPI transactions automatically expire after 2 hours
options.explanationWrong: Settled UPI payments are instant and do not auto-expire.

options.text: It lowers your monthly account fees
options.explanationWrong: Quick reporting is about fund recovery, not fee discounts.

questions.explanationCorrect: Banks coordinate between remitter and beneficiary banks using your transaction ID—acting fast preserves a better chance of recovery.

questions.prompt: How can you reduce the risk of wrong UPI transfers in the first place?

options.text: Verify the recipient's registered bank name on the confirmation screen before entering your PIN
Save only the first four digits of phone numbers
options.explanationWrong: Partial numbers raise the risk of picking the wrong contact.

options.text: Disable transaction alerts so the app runs faster
options.explanationWrong: Keep alerts enabled so you catch errors immediately.

options.text: Use the same PIN for every banking app
options.explanationWrong: Checking the payee name before PIN entry prevents wrong-person sends.

questions.explanationCorrect: Always check the verified banking name shown above the Pay button before typing your UPI PIN.
